subject: Dedicated capacity: reserve scenario analysis & GPU blend recommendation
messages:
From: Karen Lee <karen@orionhealthtech.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orionhealthtech.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — can you run scenarios on our workload?

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed by the predictable latency and fallbacks. Procurement asked me to get a detailed sizing worksheet so we can decide between a 12-month committed pool vs a hybrid commit + burst model.

I've attached a sanitized sample of our traffic (per-minute token counts by route) and a short list of non-negotiables: 95th pct latency < 250ms for our customer-facing chat route, retention of per-token audit logs for 90 days, and the ability to burst for nightly batch indexing.

Can Redwood run 2 scenarios for us:
- Baseline: steady-state QPS at current levels (weekdays peak / weekends low).
- Hybrid: 60% commit, 40% burst capacity, include cold-start penalties and KV cache hit improvements.

If you can return recommended GPU types, a packed node count with packing factor assumptions, and a per-month committed cost vs estimated burst spend, we can take that to our finance/AP.

Thanks —
Karen
Senior Product Operations
Orion HealthTech

Attachment: orion_workload_sample.csv (csv, 45KB)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — can you run scenarios on our workload?

Hi Karen —

Appreciate the data and the clear constraints. We'll run the two scenario families you requested and return a short spreadsheet with:
- GPU mix candidates (H100-80GB, A100-80GB, and an 8-bit quantized H100 variant)
- Assumed packing factors for multi-tenant vs single-tenant models
- Burst profile assumptions (concurrent streams and token/s vs tokens/min)
- Cost delta table (committed monthly vs estimated burst)
- Risk notes (cold-start windows, KV cache warmup, and SLA implications)

Marcus will sketch the topology and packing; Priyom will model throughput and unit economics. Expect the workbook and an annotated summary by Friday EOD PT.

One quick ask — can you confirm the percent of requests that require full-context (>2048 tokens) vs short context (<512 tokens)? That helps select kernel profiles.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, Karen Lee <karen@orionhealthtech.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: GPU blend / packing sketch for Orion scenarios

Team / Karen,

I've run a quick topology exercise against the sample and sketched three candidate blends with packing heuristics. High-level notes below — full calculations are in the attached workbook.

Option Alpha — H100-first, performance priority
- Recommended hardware: H100-80GB instances for the chat route and batch workers for nightly indexing.
- Assumed average sequence length: 1,100 tokens (using Karen's sample).
- Packing factor: 1.6x (we can safely co-locate up to 60% more short/medium requests on each GPU with dynamic batching).
- Throughput: ~1.8M tokens / GPU / hour for chat under continuous load.
- Latency SLO headroom: comfortable for p95 < 200ms at provisioned concurrency.

Option Beta — Cost-balanced (A100 + H100 mix)
- 60% A100-80GB, 40% H100-80GB in committed pool. A100s handle lower priority background workloads and embeddings; H100s reserved for low-latency chat.
- Packing factor: 1.4x across mixed workloads.
- Throughput: combined effective throughput ~1.3M tokens / GPU / hour on committed pool.

Option Gamma — Quantized-heavy (density-first)
- Use quantized variants of the model on H100 with 4-bit kernels for background workloads and a smaller set of H100 full-precision GPUs for chat.
- Packing factor: 2.0x for quantized background.
- Tradeoff: ~20% lower per-token quality risk on retrieval-augmented prompts; largest cost savings on committed CU.

Operational considerations:
- Warm KV cache reduces steady-state token cost by reducing repeated attention through prefix caching for sessions. We estimate a 12–18% effective token reduction on chat routes after warm-up.
- Burst capacity should be modeled as a p95 concurrency spike; recommend sizing burst reserve for 3x baseline peak to avoid queueing during nightly index jobs.

I'll attach a topology diagram and the packing sheet.

Marcus Lin
Sr. Infra Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_reserve_scenarios_20270401.xlsx (xlsx, 320KB)

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Karen Lee <karen@orionhealthtech.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Cost / throughput model outputs (first-pass)

Karen —

I ran the sample against our cost model. Key outputs (first-pass, numbers rounded):

Scenario: Baseline (100% committed)
- Recommended committed pool: 18 x H100-80GB nodes (packing factor 1.6)
- Expected steady throughput: ~32M tokens/hour across pool (chat + embeddings + background).
- Estimated committed monthly cost: $178,000
- Expected burst spend (low frequency scaling to match peak): +$22,000/mo on average

Scenario: Hybrid (60% commit, 40% burst)
- Committed pool: 11 x H100 + 4 x A100 (handles embeddings and lower-priority tasks)
- Estimated committed monthly cost: $122,000
- Average burst consumption (on-demand H100 equivalent): $48,000/mo (depends on nights + unexpected spikes)
- Net-expected monthly variance vs Baseline: ~+/- $10k depending on burst smoothing and caching improvements.

Notes and assumptions:
- We assumed a 12% KV cache effective token savings for chat after steady-state warmup; if cache is disabled, burst spend increases by ~15%.
- Cold-start penalty modeled as an extra 150–300ms for first requests to a cold model shard; impacts p95 unless you keep a tiny warm pool (recommended 2 nodes).
- We included network egress for embeddings at $0.02 per 1k vectors as a conservative line item (your region confirmed as US West).

Next steps:
- If Orion confirms the committed % and acceptable monthly budget band, we'll produce a final SOW and a recommended rollout (canary commit -> full commit).
- I can also produce a side-by-side DocuSign-ready order form with the 12-month discounted commit vs month-to-month hybrid pricing.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: gpu_mix_cost_model_A100_H100.csv (csv, 28KB)

Tessa / team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the detailed workbook. This level of visibility is exactly what finance needed. A couple quick clarifications before we escalate to budget: 

1) Sequence-length split: approximately 22% >2048 tokens, 63% between 512–2048, 15% <512.
2) Nightly indexing runs for 90 minutes at 3x baseline token/s concentrated between 02:00–03:30 local time.
3) We are highly sensitive to p95 latency for chat — procurement will push to ensure the committed pool covers 95% of observed peaks.

We'll review the workbook with finance and loop back with our committed % preference (likely leaning to Hybrid to preserve cash flow). Please leave the DocuSign placeholder open; procurement may request an exception for a 9-month commit.

Appreciate it —
Karen
